title: Unique lifts of simplex arrows to the generators-and-relations presentation
statement: Use the presentation category of [lem-sc-module-cup-godement-simplex-presentation-faithful], with its full definition recalled here. Let $P$ have objects $[n]$ for $n\geq0$ and arrows finite composable words in generators $\delta_i:[n-1]\to[n]$ ($n\geq1$, $0\leq i\leq n$) and $\sigma_i:[n+1]\to[n]$ ($0\leq i\leq n$), modulo the category congruence generated by $\delta_j\circ\delta_i=\delta_i\circ\delta_{j-1}$ for $i<j$, $\sigma_j\circ\delta_i=\delta_i\circ\sigma_{j-1}$ for $i<j$, $\sigma_j\circ\delta_j=1=\sigma_j\circ\delta_{j+1}$, $\sigma_j\circ\delta_i=\delta_{i-1}\circ\sigma_j$ for $i>j+1$, and $\sigma_j\circ\sigma_i=\sigma_i\circ\sigma_{j+1}$ for $i\leq j$, with degree superscripts suppressed and only typed instances imposed. Let $\Delta$ be the category with objects $[n]=\{0<\cdots<n\}$ and order-preserving maps [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], and let $J:P\to\Delta$ fix these object labels and send $\delta_i$ to the increasing injection omitting $i$ and $\sigma_i$ to the nondecreasing surjection taking the value $i$ twice. Every arrow $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ in $\Delta$ has a unique lift $\widehat\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ in $P$ with $J(\widehat\alpha)=\alpha$. These lifts satisfy $\widehat{1}=1$, $\widehat{\beta\circ\alpha}=\widehat\beta\circ\widehat\alpha$, and the lift of each coface or codegeneracy is the corresponding generator. Thus the assignments $[n]\mapsto[n]$ and $\alpha\mapsto\widehat\alpha$ define a functor $K:\Delta\to P$ with $J\circ K=\mathrm{id}_{\Delta}$ and $K\circ J=\mathrm{id}_P$.

proof.text: For $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ define $W(\alpha)$ to mean that there exists $f:[m]\to[n]$ in $P$ with $J(f)=\alpha$. The identity has witness $1_{[m]}$. If $f,g$ witness $W(\alpha),W(\beta)$ for composable arrows, then $g\circ f$ witnesses $W(\beta\circ\alpha)$, since $J$ is a functor. Each coface and codegeneracy has its corresponding generator as witness, by the stipulated action of $J$. Thus $W$ contains identities and generators and is closed under composition.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-simplex-morphism-property-generators] to this property $W$ of morphisms of $\Delta$. Step 1 verifies all its hypotheses, so $W(\alpha)$ holds for every $\alpha$. Hence every simplex arrow has a lift with exactly the specified source and target.

proof.text: If $f,g:[m]\to[n]$ are two lifts of the same $\alpha$, then $J(f)=\alpha=J(g)$. The faithfulness assertion of [lem-sc-module-cup-godement-simplex-presentation-faithful] gives $f=g$. Together with step 2 this proves existence and uniqueness; denote the unique lift by $\widehat\alpha$.

source.place: Tag 0168, lemma-face-degeneracy-category (a),(c); Tag 016B, lemma-characterize-simplicial-object (2). The omitted argument is supplied using the existing generation and faithfulness nodes.

proof.text: The arrows $1$, $\widehat\beta\circ\widehat\alpha$, and each presentation generator have images respectively $1$, $\beta\circ\alpha$, and its associated coface or codegeneracy. Uniqueness from step 3 identifies them with the corresponding unique lifts. These identities give the functor laws for $K([n])=[n]$, $K(\alpha)=\widehat\alpha$. On objects $JK$ and $KJ$ are identities. On arrows $JK(\alpha)=\alpha$ by construction; for $f$ in $P$, both $KJ(f)$ and $f$ lift $J(f)$, so uniqueness gives $KJ(f)=f$. These are strict equalities of functors.
